# Configuration

<!-- Generated by `bin/portico-gateway export-config-doc` from `gateway/portico_gateway/config_doc.py`; edit there, not here. -->

Two files in the state folder (`~/.portico/` unless `PORTICO_HOME` or `--state` says otherwise) configure
the gateway, and both are optional:

- **`config.toml`** is the deployment's: what every person using it gets. An update may replace it.
- **`config.local.toml`**, beside it, is the person's own overrides. Nothing writes it but the person (or an
  agent they ask). Tables merge key by key; any other value, arrays included, replaces the deployment's
  (a local `[[services]]` list replaces the whole list). Any key may be overridden.

The merged result is checked as one file; an error names the file and the key, and an invalid file stops
the gateway from starting (`bin/doctor` says why). A deployment that keeps its `config.toml` in a git
repository adds `config.local.toml` to that repository's `.gitignore`.

## For an agent asked to "change X for me"

1. Put a person's change in `config.local.toml`; put the deployment's change in `config.toml`.
2. Run `bin/portico-gateway config show` before and after (`--changed` for only what differs from the
   defaults, `--json` to read it). Each key shows its value in force and where it came from:
   `[default]`, `[config.toml]` or `[config.local.toml]`.
3. Say what the change needs: most keys apply after a gateway restart (`bin/portico-gateway stop`; the app
   starts a fresh one and says when one is needed); the entries below say which apply sooner or later.
4. Never edit `config.toml` for a personal preference.


## General (top-level keys)

### `setting_sources`

Which Claude Code settings the agent loads: `user`, `project` (the folder's CLAUDE.md, skills, hooks), `local`. Never empty: an empty list drops the folder's instructions and hooks.

- **Type:** list of text · **Default:** `["project"]`
- **Example:** `setting_sources = ["user", "project"]`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `before_first_chat`

A command (/bin/sh -c) run once per launch before the first engine starts.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `before_first_chat = "bin/prepare"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `on_stop`

A command (/bin/sh -c) run on the way out, when the gateway stops.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `on_stop = "bin/cleanup"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `command_timeout_seconds`

How long a deployment command (before_first_chat, on_stop, restarts, update) may run. At least 1.

- **Type:** whole number · **Default:** `120`
- **Example:** `command_timeout_seconds = 120`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `default_folder`

Where a new session works when the person has not chosen a folder.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `default_folder = "~/work"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** either: the deployment sets a default, a person often overrides it

### `card_hold_seconds`

How long a permission card waits with no app attached before it is denied; 0 denies at once.

- **Type:** whole number · **Default:** `600`
- **Example:** `card_hold_seconds = 600`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `history_buffer`

Events kept per chat so a reconnecting app catches up. At least 1.

- **Type:** whole number · **Default:** `2000`
- **Example:** `history_buffer = 2000`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `presentation`

`"single"`: one live session at a time, renewed; `"multiple"`: a list of chats.

- **Type:** one of "single", "multiple" · **Default:** `"single"`
- **Example:** `presentation = "single"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `log_prompt`

The log step (Log session, /log, and a renewal first), sent as a message; unset means no log step.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `log_prompt = "/session-close"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `plugins`

Plug-in modules, imported at start.

- **Type:** list of text · **Default:** `[]`
- **Example:** `plugins = ["my_deployment_plugin"]`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `plugin_paths`

Absolute folders put on the import path for the plug-ins (outside the checkout).

- **Type:** list of text · **Default:** `[]`
- **Example:** `plugin_paths = ["~/my-plugins"]`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `permission_mode`

A new session's mode: `"auto"` (the engine's classifier decides), `"acceptEdits"` (file edits allowed), `"default"` (ask each time).

- **Type:** one of "default", "acceptEdits", "auto" · **Default:** `"auto"`
- **Example:** `permission_mode = "auto"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** either: the deployment sets a default, a person often overrides it

### `services_interval_seconds`

How often the [[services]] checks run. At least 5.

- **Type:** whole number · **Default:** `30`
- **Example:** `services_interval_seconds = 30`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `titles`

`"generated"`: after a session's first clean turn a small model names it; `"first_line"`: the first line of the first message, no extra model call.

- **Type:** one of "generated", "first_line" · **Default:** `"generated"`
- **Example:** `titles = "generated"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** either: the deployment sets a default, a person often overrides it

### `title_model`

The model for generated titles; unset is "haiku", the provider's small model.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `title_model = "my-small-model"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `system_prompt`

`"claude_code"` (or `"default"`): Claude Code's own prompt, which updates with Claude Code. `"custom"`: system_prompt_file's text is the whole prompt. `"none"` (legacy): the SDK's empty prompt. Portico's own lines always come last.

- **Type:** one of "claude_code", "custom", "none" · **Default:** `"claude_code"`
- **Example:** `system_prompt = "custom"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart; the prompt then applies to the next new or renewed session (a running session keeps its prompt until it compacts)
- **Belongs in:** either: the deployment sets a default, a person often overrides it

### `system_prompt_file`

The whole prompt, as an absolute path, required with system_prompt = "custom" and ignored otherwise. Read at each engine start. `bin/portico-gateway capture-prompt` makes a starting copy.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `system_prompt_file = "~/prompts/mine.md"`
- **Applies:** the file's text: the next new or renewed session; the key itself: gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** commonly a personal override in `config.local.toml`

### `system_prompt_append`

An absolute path to text added after the prompt, in any mode. Read at each engine start.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `system_prompt_append = "~/my-deployment/prompt.md"`
- **Applies:** the file's text: the next new or renewed session; the key itself: gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `login_shell_path`

The engine gets the person's login-shell PATH first, so it finds npx, node, uvx; false keeps the inherited PATH.

- **Type:** true/false · **Default:** `true`
- **Example:** `login_shell_path = true`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

## [brand]

### `brand.name`

The product name the app shows.

- **Type:** text · **Default:** `"Portico"`
- **Example:** `name = "Acme"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `brand.agent_name`

What the agent is called in the app.

- **Type:** text · **Default:** `"Agent"`
- **Example:** `agent_name = "Ace"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `brand.accent`

The accent colour, CSS hex.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `accent = "#3B6EF5"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `brand.icon`

An image for the mark; a flat square is rounded in the macOS icon shape.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `icon = "/path/to/icon.png"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `brand.header_image`

An absolute path to an image that replaces the mark and name in the toolbar, 28 pt tall (SVG or PDF stays sharp).

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `header_image = "/path/to/lockup.svg"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `brand.version`

The deployment's version; the About panel shows it in place of the app's.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `version = "1.4.0"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `brand.about`

The About panel's text under the version; {app_version} and {built} are filled in, "" shows nothing.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `about = "Questions: help@example.com"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `brand.app_icon`

A 1024×1024 PNG for the app bundle (bin/install); never sent to the app.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `app_icon = "~/icons/app.png"`
- **Applies:** reinstall (bin/install)
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `brand.app_icon_assets`

A precompiled asset catalog (Assets.car) for the app bundle; with app_icon_name.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `app_icon_assets = "~/icons/Assets.car"`
- **Applies:** reinstall (bin/install)
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `brand.app_icon_name`

The icon's name inside app_icon_assets.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `app_icon_name = "AppIcon"`
- **Applies:** reinstall (bin/install)
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

## [update]

### `update.check`

A command that exits 0 and prints a version when an update is available; exit 1 or no output means none; any other exit is a failed check.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `check = "my-tool update --check"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `update.run`

A command that performs the update; the app's Update available runs it.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `run = "my-tool update"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

## [deployment]

### `deployment.restart`

One command that restarts all the deployment's services (Restart all services).

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `restart = "my-tool restart-all"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `deployment.status`

One command printing {"services": [...]} rows that replace the [[services]] checks.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `status = "my-tool status --json"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

## [[actions]]

### `actions`

Buttons in the input bar; each sends its text.

- **Type:** list of tables · **Default:** `[]`
- **Example:** `[[actions]] label = "Review", text = "/review"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** either: the deployment sets a default, a person often overrides it

### `actions[].label`

The button's label.

- **Type:** text · **Default:** `required`
- **Example:** `label = "Review"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** either: the deployment sets a default, a person often overrides it

### `actions[].text`

What the button sends.

- **Type:** text · **Default:** `required`
- **Example:** `text = "/review"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** either: the deployment sets a default, a person often overrides it

## [[services]]

### `services`

What the deployment depends on, shown in the app's services menu.

- **Type:** list of tables · **Default:** `[]`
- **Example:** `[[services]] id = "memory", name = "Memory", check = "…"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `services[].id`

Unique; lowercase letters, digits and dashes.

- **Type:** text · **Default:** `required`
- **Example:** `id = "memory"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `services[].name`

The name the menu shows.

- **Type:** text · **Default:** `required`
- **Example:** `name = "Memory"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `services[].check`

A command (/bin/sh -c): exit 0 is up, 75 is stuck, anything else down.

- **Type:** text · **Default:** `required`
- **Example:** `check = "curl -sf http://localhost:8888/health"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `services[].restart`

A command the menu's Restart runs.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `restart = "my-tool restart memory"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `services[].up_detail`

A line shown while it is up.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `up_detail = "recall and capture"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `services[].timeout_seconds`

The check is killed after this. At least 1.

- **Type:** whole number · **Default:** `10`
- **Example:** `timeout_seconds = 10`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

## [[roots]]

### `roots`

Folders the Files pane can browse.

- **Type:** list of tables · **Default:** `[]`
- **Example:** `[[roots]] name = "projects", path = "~/projects"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** either: the deployment sets a default, a person often overrides it

### `roots[].name`

The folder's name in the pane.

- **Type:** text · **Default:** `required`
- **Example:** `name = "projects"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** either: the deployment sets a default, a person often overrides it

### `roots[].path`

An absolute path; a leading ~ is expanded.

- **Type:** text · **Default:** `required`
- **Example:** `path = "~/projects"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** either: the deployment sets a default, a person often overrides it

## [sessions]

### `sessions.next_number`

A command whose output is the next session's number.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `next_number = "my-tool next-session"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `sessions.lock_folder`

True fixes "Works in" to the deployment's folder.

- **Type:** true/false · **Default:** `false`
- **Example:** `lock_folder = false`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

## [threads]

### `threads.max`

Threads open beside Main, 0 to 2; 0 turns threads off.

- **Type:** whole number · **Default:** `2`
- **Example:** `max = 2`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** either: the deployment sets a default, a person often overrides it

## [files]

### `files.hide_session_folder`

True lists only the [[roots]] in the Files pane, not the session's own folder.

- **Type:** true/false · **Default:** `false`
- **Example:** `hide_session_folder = false`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** either: the deployment sets a default, a person often overrides it

## [viewer]

### `viewer.agent_can_see`

The default for Settings › Agent can see the viewer.

- **Type:** true/false · **Default:** `true`
- **Example:** `agent_can_see = true`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** either: the deployment sets a default, a person often overrides it

### `viewer.agent_checks_html`

The default for Settings › Agent checks HTML it creates.

- **Type:** true/false · **Default:** `true`
- **Example:** `agent_checks_html = true`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** either: the deployment sets a default, a person often overrides it

### `viewer.act_hosts`

Outside sites the agent may click and type on (bare host names; subdomains included).

- **Type:** list of text · **Default:** `[]`
- **Example:** `act_hosts = ["figma.com"]`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `viewer.properties`

How a Markdown page's Properties first open: `"folded"` or `"open"`.

- **Type:** one of "folded", "open" · **Default:** `"folded"`
- **Example:** `properties = "folded"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** either: the deployment sets a default, a person often overrides it

## [links]

### `links.sites`

Host (or a parent domain) to the name a link chip shows.

- **Type:** table of text · **Default:** `{}`
- **Example:** `sites = { "tracker.example.com" = "Tracker" }`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

## [apps]

### `apps.enabled`

MCP Apps: a tool's page shown in the chat; false keeps every tool a plain row.

- **Type:** true/false · **Default:** `true`
- **Example:** `enabled = true`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

## [mcp]

### `mcp.core`

Servers in the folder's .mcp.json that are part of the deployment itself.

- **Type:** list of text · **Default:** `[]`
- **Example:** `core = ["tracker"]`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

## [spaces]

### `spaces.folder`

A folder of pages the agent keeps current; must exist. Unset: <state dir>/spaces.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `folder = "~/Spaces"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** either: the deployment sets a default, a person often overrides it

### `spaces.refresh`

A command run for Refresh, with $PORTICO_SPACE set.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `refresh = "my-tool refresh-space"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `spaces.remove`

A command run after a space's file is moved to the Trash.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `remove = "my-tool forget-space"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `spaces.act`

A command for space-action: links, with $PORTICO_ACTION and $PORTICO_ITEM.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `act = "my-tool space-action"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `spaces.require_folder`

A page is a space only with a folder of its name beside it.

- **Type:** true/false · **Default:** `false`
- **Example:** `require_folder = true`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

## [person]

### `person.name`

The person's real name for comments; unset uses the computer's full user name.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `name = "Sam Rivera"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** commonly a personal override in `config.local.toml`

## [voice]

### `voice.read_aloud`

Read aloud on each reply: true shows the switch in Settings; the person's on/off choice stays in the app.

- **Type:** true/false · **Default:** `false`
- **Example:** `read_aloud = true`
- **Applies:** gateway restart (the app follows when it reconnects)
- **Belongs in:** commonly a personal override in `config.local.toml`

## [signin]

### `signin.aws-sso.patterns`

Regular expressions (case-insensitive) that make a failed turn an expired AWS sign-in. Unset: `cloud_credential_error`, "Could not load AWS credentials", "SSO session .* has expired".

- **Type:** list of text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `patterns = ["cloud_credential_error"]`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `signin.aws-sso.check`

A command that exits 0 once the sign-in is current again, run every 10 s while a turn waits. Unset: the AWS SSO token cache (~/.aws/sso/cache), read every 5 s.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `check = "my-tool signed-in"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `signin.aws-sso.open`

The command the card's Open sign-in page runs; its output's first URL and code show under Trouble signing in?. Unset: no button.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `open = "aws sso login --profile work"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `signin.aws-sso.title`

The card's title. Unset: "Sign in again to continue".

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `title = "Sign in again to continue"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `signin.aws-sso.body`

The card's text. Unset: "Your sign-in to AWS has run out. Sign in in your browser; this conversation carries on by itself when you're done."

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `body = "Your sign-in to AWS has run out."`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `signin.aws-sso.sso_start_url`

The SSO start URL whose cached token counts as signed in again. Unset: any.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `sso_start_url = "https://example.awsapps.com/start"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `signin.claude.patterns`

Regular expressions (case-insensitive) that make a failed turn an expired Claude sign-in. Unset: `^authentication_failed$`, "Login expired", "OAuth token revoked", "OAuth token has expired", "Not logged in".

- **Type:** list of text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `patterns = ["^authentication_failed$"]`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `signin.claude.check`

A command that exits 0 once the sign-in is current again, run every 10 s while a turn waits. Unset: `claude auth status` (signed in with claude.ai).

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `check = "claude auth status"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `signin.claude.open`

The command the card's Open sign-in page runs; its URL shows under Trouble signing in?, with a field that pastes a code into it. Unset: `claude auth login`.

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `open = "claude auth login"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `signin.claude.title`

The card's title. Unset: "Sign in again to continue".

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `title = "Sign in again to continue"`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`

### `signin.claude.body`

The card's text. Unset: "Your Claude sign-in has run out. Sign in in your browser; this conversation carries on by itself when you're done."

- **Type:** text (optional) · **Default:** `not set`
- **Example:** `body = "Your Claude sign-in has run out."`
- **Applies:** gateway restart
- **Belongs in:** the deployment's `config.toml`
